title: Design federated collection protocol (CollectionItem)
description: A generic ActivityPub extension for curated personal collections of any type — books, records, rocks, stamps, fountain pens, pigeons, anything. Items reference Wikidata for type taxonomy and property schemas. Shelves are named groupings. Reviews/ratings attach to items. Acquisition metadata tracks provenance. Federation lets you follow someone's collection and see new additions in your feed.
design: Core types: CollectionItem (name, category wikidata URI, image, free-form properties, acquired date), Shelf (named grouping), Review/Rating (opinion on item), Acquisition (provenance: bought/found/gifted/traded, date, source). Federation: items are AP objects, adding to a shelf is a Create activity, reviews are Note objects with inReplyTo pointing at the item. Wikidata category URI is the interop key — clients can render any item generically (name+image+rating) or with type-specific UI when they recognize the category.
notes:
## Prior Art & Standards

**Museum/Cultural Heritage:**
- CIDOC-CRM (ISO 21127) — the canonical cultural heritage ontology. Models things, events, actors, places, time-spans. Every major museum system implements a subset. Extremely thorough, extremely academic, no federation story.
- LIDO (Lightweight Information Describing Objects) — XML schema for museum object exchange/harvesting
- Spectrum — UK procedural standard for collections management
- CCO (Cataloging Cultural Objects) — guidelines for visual culture
- Dublin Core — 15 generic metadata elements, baseline standard

**Domain-Specific:**
- Darwin Core — biological specimens (iNaturalist, GBIF). Has Occurrence, Taxon, Event
- Numista — coins and banknotes schema
- Discogs — vinyl/music release data model
- Getty vocabularies — AAT (Art & Architecture Thesaurus), ULAN (artist names), TGN (place names). Controlled term lists, not ontologies, but widely referenced

**Key Insight:**
CIDOC-CRM solved the hard ontology problem but is unapproachable for hobbyists. Wikidata absorbed much of its structure in a more accessible form. The CollectionItem protocol references Wikidata URIs instead of building a new ontology — it's what CIDOC-CRM would look like designed for the web instead of museum registrars.

**The gap we fill:**
CIDOC-CRM has no federation story. Darwin Core has no social layer. No existing standard covers "follow my collection and see when I add something." That's the ActivityPub piece.

**Hobbyist reality:**
No universal standard exists. Collectors use spreadsheets or niche apps (Colnect for stamps, Delcampe for postcards, MyFigureCollection for anime figures) that each reinvent their own schema. A generic federated protocol could unify these.
